entries.subject: DAMIT 175: selected shape and spin
entries.finding: The official DAMIT metadata export was joined by model and asteroid identity and compared with the selected local recipe shape/model-175.txt. Model 175, version 2007-09-21, pole (200°, 52°), period 6.441111 h match the retained metadata. The archive diameter field is 93 ±9 km; its applicability to our scale is a separate calibration decision. This comparison checks source identity and metadata, not fresh mesh bytes, registration or the completeness of other archives.

entries.subject: A. Marciniak (2007), Photometry and models of selected main belt asteroids. IV. 184 Dejopeja, 276 Adelheid, 556 Phyllis
entries.finding: [A. Marciniak (2007), Photometry and models of selected main belt asteroids. IV. 184 Dejopeja, 276 Adelheid, 556 Phyllis](https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2007A%26A...473..633M) — original model publication record.

entries.subject: AKARI thermal diameter as an alternative scale
entries.finding: [AKARI AcuA](https://data.darts.isas.jaxa.jp/pub/akari/AKARI-IRC_Catalogue_AllSky_AcuA_1.0/) — retained for comparison; the documented physical calibration supplies the selected scale. Its fitted nonrotating-sphere diameter is 64.9 ± 0.9 km. Formal catalog error omits additional shape, spin and thermal-model effects; no total confidence interval is invented. The original catalogue row for asteroid 184 was retrieved again and matched field-for-field with the retained row, including diameter, reported error and detection count.
entries.revisitWhen: A source-specific comparison with the selected shape and physical calibration justifies changing the adopted scale.

entries.subject: Hanuš et al. (2013), Keck AO volume-equivalent diameters
entries.finding: [Hanuš et al. (2013), Keck AO volume-equivalent diameters](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1308.0446) — retained primary publication; see the body-specific selection and calibration above.

entries.subject: Shape and spin alternatives
entries.finding: Alternative archive solutions: model 176, pole ['18', '54'], [Model 176](https://damit.cuni.cz/projects/damit/asteroid_models/view/176) The live DAMIT export lists these other models for this target: 176: pole (18°, 54°), 6.44111 h, version 2007-09-21, archive diameter 95 km. These are archive alternatives, not necessarily newly released models or preferred replacements. Comparing their source methods and any pole-specific calibration remains necessary before changing the selected mesh.
entries.revisitWhen: A released numerical replacement or independent pole/size constraints that distinguish the recorded alternatives, followed by comparison against the currently selected model.

entries.subject: PDS SBN catalogue values that disagree with the factsheet or are not shown
entries.finding: The display scale "46.5 km (size-calibrated model)" (damit-models) implies a diameter of 93 km, outside the added NEOWISE V2.0 neowise_mainbelt.csv record 141 (Masiero et al. 2014) diameter 62.483 ± 0.320 km (NEOWISE, NEATM). Both are shown; the display scale is not changed.
entries.revisitWhen: A newer release of the named catalogue, or a review that replaces the shown value.
